liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the Sugaree and Stagger Lee performances in the first set cook strongly; Reviewer found the Sugaree jam calming and nice [7][18]
- **All Along The Watchtower** (2 reviews): Reviewer found the band playing Watchtower while lightning and clouds closed in a truly magical moment; Reviewer recalls the band jamming Watchtower through the lightning, thunder and clouds, as if the music broke up the storm [7][9]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): First-timer says the opening Hell In A Bucket frightened them [18]
- **Walkin' Blues** (1 review): Reviewer disliked the slide guitar work in Walkin' Blues [18]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry's jam in Stagger Lee is great and seems to go on forever [11]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry's jam in Music Never Stopped is great and seems endless [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-06-18.AKG451.Darby.119660.Flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1993-06-18.schoeps.evans.triportweek.33932.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 155 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Front-of-board-area audience recording with audible crowd chatter, clapping and yelling, though still very listenable [3]
- **gd93-06-18.sbd.miller.13784.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 149 min; rated 3.88/5 by 25 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound of this soundboard recording nice [8]
- **gd1993-06-18.AKG451.Darby.119661.Flac1644**: audience recording; 18 songs; 156 min [2]

## Around the show

- A thunderstorm blew in off Lake Michigan during Drums/Space, with lightning and clouds over the lit Chicago skyline behind the stadium [7]
- Storm began pouring during the show; the reviewer's friend Jason disappeared and was found a week later at a truck stop three states away [8]
- Storm rolled in with lightning, thunder and clouds; reviewer was tripping and this was their last Chicago and East Coast run before moving west [9]
- From high in the end zone, the stadium looked like a spaceship pushing through the skyline, with show reflections bouncing off low clouds [11]
- Reviewer got a spare ticket at 30 minutes' notice and drove from Little Rock, Arkansas; remembers the storm and clouds spilling in [12]
- Reviewer sheltered under the third level and saw lightning strike the Sears tower; a friend nicknamed Coyote went missing that night [15]
- Chicago local says Soldier Field offered parks and the lake to explore, plus a shakedown street vending area, and Heads impressed onlookers peacefully [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-06-18.AKG451.Darby.119660.Flac1648**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: flac16/48kHz ; Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; AKG451EB/CK1's (DIN/OTS Section 1 Row 30 Seat 7)> Whirlwind Phantoms>Teac DA-P20 @ 16/48; Transfer… [1]
- **gd1993-06-18.schoeps.evans.triportweek.33932.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Todd Evans, Adam Gross and Bill Pobega; transferred by 48K >> 44.1 resampling (audacity 1.2.3), tracking (shntool 2.0.3) and flac16 encoding (flac 1.1.2) running on FC3 linux by triportweek.; source: Schoeps CMC321 (Sub Cardiods) -> Oade Power Supply -> Panasonic sv255 - 7' Stand [3]. Also: Schoeps-mic recording by Evans, unedited apart from trimmed dead air before each set; part of Lossless Legs GEMS project [3]
- **gd93-06-18.sbd.miller.13784.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>Dat>Samplitude>Cool Edit Pro>CD [5]
- **gd1993-06-18.AKG451.Darby.119661.Flac1644**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; AKG451EB/CK1's (DIN/OTS Section 1 Row 30 Seat 7)> Whirlwind Phantoms>Teac DA-P20 @ 16/48; Transfer Information:Sony… [2]
